key_insight: Changing the source-to-substrate distance during thermal evaporation systematically tunes the thickness, band gap, and transport behavior of CdTe, CdSe, and Sb2S3 thin films.
engineering_relevance: CdTe and CdSe show low band gaps and strong absorption, making them promising absorber-layer candidates for thin-film solar cells, while Sb2S3 provides a comparative wide-band-gap reference.
method: Thermal evaporation deposition of CdTe, CdSe, and Sb2S3 thin films
Varied source-to-substrate distance from 15 to 24 cm
Characterized structure, composition, optical response, and electrical behavior using XRD, EDX, and optical/electrical measurements
evidence_signal: The abstract reports polycrystalline CdTe/CdSe, amorphous Sb2S3, thickness reduction with increasing distance, and only marginal band-gap shifts, with all films showing semiconducting behavior.
watch_item: Results are based on a limited SSD range and thin-film characterization only, so device-level solar-cell performance still needs direct validation.
paper_title: Effect of Source-to-Substrate Distance on the Optical and Electrical Properties of Thermally Deposited CdTe, CdSe and Sb$_2$S$_3$ Thin Films
